mainTopic: The number of lashes, the rules of assessing a person's strength (אומד), and the procedure of מלקות
overview: The amud opens with the end of a משנה about re-assessing how many lashes a person can survive. The גמרא explains that the חכמים give thirty-nine lashes because the פסוק says 'a number close to forty.' רבא learns from this that a great scholar deserves the same honor people give a ספר תורה. רבי יצחק brings a פסוק from זכריה as the source for רבי יהודה's full forty, and the רבנן explain that it is about schoolchildren. The גמרא then reads the משנה closely to learn that a new assessment exempts him only after real lashes. רב ששת settles a clash with a ברייתא by splitting a same-day assessment from a later-day one. A new משנה covers one sin with two לאוין, and רב ששת explains when one assessment can cover both, forty-one or forty-two. The last משנה describes how מלקות is given: the post, the strap, the פסוקים read aloud, and when the lashes stop early.

steps.title: The end of the משנה: re-assessing the person in the middle of lashes
steps.stepSummary: The משנה finishes its rules on assessment: if a new assessment changes the number midway, he is פטור from more lashes.
steps.simpleTranslation: If they then assessed that he cannot take forty, he is exempt. If they first assessed that he could take eighteen, and after he was flogged they assessed that he could take forty, he is also exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: These are the closing lines of the משנה. They teach that once lashes are given based on one assessment, a later change in the assessment does not bring more lashes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two cases appear here. In the first, a weaker assessment midway ends the lashes. In the second, the person was assessed at eighteen and received them, and even if he now looks strong enough for forty, he is פטור because his punishment was already carried out.

keyTerms.meaning: Assessing how many lashes a person can survive
Exempt; no more lashes are given
And once he was flogged

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמְדוּ שֶׁאֵין יָכוֹל לְקַבֵּל אַרְבָּעִים – פָּטוּר.
phrases.english: And then they assessed that he cannot receive forty, he is exempt.
If they assessed him as able to receive eighteen,
and once he was flogged, they assessed
that he is able to receive forty, he is exempt.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: Once lashes are given according to an assessment, a later reassessment in either direction does not bring more lashes.

steps.title: Why only thirty-nine lashes?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins by asking for the reason the חכמים say thirty-nine and not forty.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens with a question. It is setting up the next step, which will explain why the חכמים count only thirty-nine lashes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier the משנה said a person gets forty minus one, while the פסוק says 'forty.' The גמרא wants to know where that missing lash comes from.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?

phrases.english: Gemara: What is the reason?
phrases.notes: He means: why do the חכמים say thirty-nine, as the משנה taught earlier?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts the גמרא's analysis of the משנה
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source for giving thirty-nine lashes instead of forty

steps.title: Reading the word order of the verse: a count that comes close to forty
steps.stepSummary: The word order 'במספר ארבעים' teaches a count that comes up to forty, which means thirty-nine.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the verse had said 'forty by number,' I would say it means exactly forty. Now that it says 'by number, forty,' it means a number that comes up to forty.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers from the order of the words in the פסוק. Because 'by number' comes right before 'forty,' it means a count leading up to forty, not forty itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'במספר' and 'ארבעים' sit next to each other across two פסוקים. Read together, they describe a number that reaches toward forty and stops just short of it, so the count is thirty-nine.

keyTerms.meaning: By number
I would have said (a first impression that turns out wrong)
Reaches up to; adds up toward

steps.confusionAlert: The verse does not say 'thirty-nine.' The חכמים learn it from the order of the words, reading 'by number' as attached to 'forty.'

phrases.english: If it had been written "forty by number,"
I would have said: forty as an exact count;
now that it is written "by number, forty,"
phrases.notes: דברים 25:2–3. 'By number' ends one פסוק and 'forty' begins the next.

phrases.english: it means a count that comes up to forty.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The word order 'במספר ארבעים' means a number approaching forty, which is thirty-nine.
steps.whatToRemember: The thirty-nine lashes come from reading 'במספר ארבעים' as 'a number close to forty.'

steps.title: רבא: people should stand for a great Torah scholar
steps.stepSummary: רבא learns from the thirty-nine lashes that a תלמיד חכם deserves at least the honor given to a ספר תורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: How foolish are other people who stand up for a Torah scroll but not for a great man. In the Torah scroll it says forty, and the Rabbis came and took away one.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא makes a lesson from what we just learned. Since the חכמים had the power to read 'forty' as thirty-nine, a great scholar deserves to be honored by standing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ספר תורה on its own says 'forty,' but the חכמים, through their reading, set the practice at thirty-nine. רבא's point is that people who honor the scroll and not the scholar have missed that the scholar is the one who shows what the scroll means.

keyTerms.meaning: Fools
Stand up before (as a sign of respect)
A great man; a great Torah scholar
Reduced; subtracted

steps.whyThisMatters: This statement shows how much weight the תורה שבעל פה carries. It is also a source for the respect owed to תלמידי חכמים.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רָבָא: כַּמָּה טַפְשָׁאֵי שְׁאָר אִינָשֵׁי,
phrases.english: Rava said: How foolish are the rest of the people,
who stand up before a Torah scroll,
but do not stand up before a great man,
for in the Torah scroll "forty" is written,
and the Rabbis came and subtracted one.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: כַּמָּה טַפְשָׁאֵי שְׁאָר אִינָשֵׁי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds a lesson about honoring scholars on top of the derivation of thirty-nine
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A great Torah scholar deserves the honor of standing, since the חכמים decide how the written Torah is applied.

steps.title: רבי יצחק's source for רבי יהודה's full forty
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק brings a פסוק in זכריה about wounds 'between your hands' as the source for רבי יהודה's extra lash.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: רבי יהודה says a full forty. רבי יצחק said: What is רבי יהודה's reason? Because it is written: 'What are these wounds between your hands? And he will say: Those with which I was struck in the house of my friends.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now turns to רבי יהודה in the משנה, who says forty full lashes. רבי יצחק gives his source: a פסוק describing wounds 'between the hands.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה holds that the fortieth lash is given between the shoulders. He reads 'wounds between your hands' as describing someone who got that extra lash in that spot, so a full forty is real practice.

keyTerms.meaning: A full forty
Etc.; the rest of the quote from the משנה
Literally 'between your hands'; read here as between the shoulders
My friends; those who love me

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: אַרְבָּעִים שְׁלֵימוֹת וְכוּ׳.
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says: A full forty, etc.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה –
phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzchak said: What is the reason of Rabbi Yehuda?
As it is written: "What are these wounds between your hands?
And he will say: Those with which I was struck in the house of my friends."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next statement in the משנה, the view of רבי יהודה
steps.raayaObject: רבי יהודה's view that forty full lashes are given, the last one between the shoulders

steps.title: How do the Rabbis read that verse?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how the רבנן, who say thirty-nine, explain the פסוק in זכריה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a short question. It is setting up the next step, which will show how the רבנן understand the פסוק that רבי יהודה used.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the פסוק really describes a lash between the shoulders, the רבנן seem to have a problem. The גמרא wants their way of reading it.

keyTerms.meaning: And the Rabbis (how do they deal with this)?

phrases.english: And the Rabbis?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how the opposing view handles the source just brought
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The רבנן's explanation of the פסוק in זכריה

steps.title: The verse is about schoolchildren
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן say the פסוק describes children hit by their teacher, not lashes from בית דין.
steps.simpleTranslation: That verse is written about schoolchildren.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that, for the רבנן, the פסוק speaks about children struck by their teacher. It has nothing to do with lashes from בית דין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the פסוק is moved to a different setting, it no longer shows an extra lash between the shoulders. So the רבנן can keep thirty-nine without contradicting it.

keyTerms.meaning: Schoolchildren; young children learning Torah with a teacher

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהודה reads the זכריה פסוק as a lash between the shoulders, which makes forty. The רבנן read it as children hit by their teacher, so they keep thirty-nine.

phrases.english: That verse, about schoolchildren,
is what it is written about.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַהוּא בְּתִינוֹקוֹת שֶׁל בֵּית רַבָּן הוּא דִּכְתִיב
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק refers to schoolchildren hit by their teacher, not to court lashes.

steps.title: Inference from the משנה: only if he was actually flogged
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה on assessment and learns from 'once he was flogged' that the exemption needs actual lashes.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: One assesses only with lashes that are fit, etc. If he was flogged, yes; if he was not flogged, no.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the משנה about assessing and makes an exact inference from its words. The exemption applies only if he actually received the lashes from the first assessment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said 'once he was flogged' and then they reassessed. So only if the lashes were already given is he פטור. If he was assessed at eighteen but not flogged yet, and is then found able to take forty, he gets the full amount.

keyTerms.meaning: Lashes that are fit, meaning a number that splits into three equal parts
He was flogged
Yes / no

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think a low assessment alone exempts him. Only lashes actually given finish his punishment.

phrases.aramaic: אֵין אוֹמְדִין אֶלָּא בְּמַכּוֹת הָרְאוּיוֹת וְכוּ׳.
phrases.english: One assesses only with lashes that are fit, etc.
phrases.notes: 'Fit' means a number that splits into three equal groups. The גמרא is pointing to the cases we saw in step 1.

phrases.english: If he was flogged, yes; if he was not flogged, no.
phrases.notes: He means: he is exempt only if the lashes were actually given.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the משנה's rules of assessment and draws an inference from their wording
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The exemption from further lashes applies only when the lashes of the first assessment were actually given.

steps.title: A ברייתא seems to exempt him without any lashes
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא where a person is exempt just because the doctors changed their assessment, even though no lashes were given yet. This seems to clash with Step 8.
steps.simpleTranslation: The גמרא raises a contradiction from a ברייתא: If doctors assessed that he can take forty lashes, and then assessed again that he cannot take forty, he is exempt. If they assessed that he can take eighteen, and then assessed again that he can take forty, he is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is attacking the rule it just learned in Step 8. It brings a ברייתא where the person is exempt only because the assessment changed, with no lashes given at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 8 the גמרא learned from 'once he was flogged' that a new assessment exempts him only after actual lashes. This ברייתא gives an exemption with no lashes mentioned. So the two sources seem to disagree about whether lashes must actually be given.

keyTerms.meaning: And they raised a contradiction: one source is set against another
They assessed him: doctors judged how many lashes he can survive
Exempt: he receives no more lashes
Eighteen: a smaller number of lashes for a weaker person

steps.confusionAlert: Even in the second case, where he now looks strong enough for forty, he is still exempt. The ברייתא does not send him back for more lashes.

phrases.english: And they raised a contradiction:
If they assessed him as able to receive forty,
and they then assessed again
that he cannot receive forty – he is exempt.
If they assessed him as able to receive eighteen,
and they then assessed him again
that he can receive forty – he is exempt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the inference of Step 8 with a contradicting ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The inference from the משנה that a changed assessment exempts him only after actual lashes.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא exempts him based on a changed assessment alone, with no lashes given.

steps.title: Today's assessment versus a later day's assessment
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת says the sources talk about different cases. The משנה is about an assessment for today, and the ברייתא is about an assessment for a later day.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת said: It is not difficult. This case is where they assessed him for that same day. That case is where they assessed him for tomorrow or for another day.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת resolves the contradiction by splitting the cases. Each source is talking about a different kind of assessment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, the assessment was for that same day, so a new result means the first one was simply a mistake; he is exempt only if he was already flogged. In the ברייתא, the assessment was for a later day, so the first assessment was correct and his body really changed; then the new result exempts him even without lashes.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult: the two sources do not really clash
For that day: lashes to be given today
For tomorrow
Another day: a later day

steps.whatToRemember: An assessment for today that changes was just a mistake, so only actual lashes exempt him. An assessment for a later day that changes reflects a real change in him, so he is exempt.

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet said: It is not difficult,
this is where they assessed him for that day,
phrases.notes: This first 'this' is the משנה from Step 8.

phrases.english: that is where they assessed him
phrases.notes: This second 'that' is the ברייתא from Step 9.

phrases.english: for tomorrow and for another day.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction of Step 9 by separating the two cases.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (אוקימתא): each source is about a different kind of assessment.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה and ברייתא seemed to describe the same case and give opposite rules.
steps.terutzMaskana: Same-day assessment changing means an error, so actual lashes are needed; later-day assessment changing means a real change, so he is exempt.

steps.title: New משנה: one sin with two prohibitions
steps.stepSummary: The new משנה teaches about someone who broke two לאוין in one act. If one assessment covered both, he is flogged once and done; if not, he is flogged, heals, and is flogged again.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: If someone did one sin that has two prohibitions, and they made one assessment for him, he is flogged and exempt. If not, he is flogged, heals, and is flogged again.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It deals with someone who deserves two sets of lashes for one act.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the doctors made one assessment for both sets of lashes together, he gets that number and is fully done. If they assessed him only for one set, he takes those lashes, waits to heal, and then gets the second set.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה
Two prohibitions, each one deserving lashes
One assessment covering both sets of lashes
He is flogged and exempt from anything more
He heals

phrases.english: MISHNA

phrases.aramaic: עָבַר עֲבֵירָה שֶׁיֵּשׁ בָּהּ שְׁנֵי לָאוִין,
phrases.english: If one committed a transgression that has two prohibitions,
and they assessed him with one assessment – he is flogged and exempt,
and if not – he is flogged and heals,
and then he is flogged again.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ עָבַר עֲבֵירָה שֶׁיֵּשׁ בָּהּ שְׁנֵי לָאוִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה on a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One assessment for two לאוין means one flogging and he is exempt; otherwise he is flogged, heals, and is flogged again.

steps.title: A ברייתא says one assessment cannot cover two prohibitions
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the משנה with a ברייתא that says we never make one assessment for two לאוין.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: But isn't it taught in a ברייתא: We do not make one assessment for two prohibitions!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by challenging the new משנה. A ברייתא seems to forbid exactly what the משנה allows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said that if one assessment covered both לאוין, he is flogged once and is exempt. The ברייתא says such a single assessment is not done at all. The גמרא will need to explain how the two fit together.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion on the משנה
We do not assess
A teaching from the time of the משנה that is not in the משנה itself

phrases.english: GEMARA
But isn't it taught:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין אוֹמְדִין אוֹמֶד אֶחָד לִשְׁנֵי לָאוִין!
phrases.english: We do not make one assessment for two prohibitions!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָתַנְיָא: אֵין אוֹמְדִין אוֹמֶד אֶחָד לִשְׁנֵי לָאוִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the משנה of Step 11 with a ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's case of one assessment for two לאוין.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא says a single assessment for two לאוין is never made, which seems to contradict the משנה.

steps.title: Forty-one versus forty-two
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת says the ברייתא is about an assessment of 41 lashes, and the משנה is about an assessment of 42.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת said: There is no contradiction. The ברייתא is talking about a case where the doctors assessed that he can take forty-one lashes. The משנה is talking about a case where they assessed that he can take forty-two.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת answers the clash between the משנה and the ברייתא from Step 12. He shows that each source is talking about a different number on the assessment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A full set of מלקות is 39, and extra lashes must come in groups of three. With 41, the two extra lashes cannot form a group of three, so he gets only 39. That covers only one לאו, and he needs a new אומד later. With 42, he gets 39 for one לאו plus 3 for the second, so one assessment really works for both.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult; the sources do not really clash
They (the doctors) assessed him, meaning they judged how many lashes he can take
Literally 'forty and one' and 'forty and two', meaning 41 and 42

steps.whatToRemember: One אומד can cover two לאוין only if the number is high enough to give a full 39 plus at least 3 more.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think 41 means 41 lashes are given. Since lashes beyond 39 must come in threes, an assessment of 41 still means only 39 lashes.

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet said: It is not difficult.
This one is where they assessed him for forty-one.
phrases.notes: 'This one' is the ברייתא that said one assessment never covers two לאוין.

phrases.english: That one is where they assessed him for forty-two.
phrases.notes: 'That one' is the משנה that allows one assessment for both לאוין.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (אוקימתא): each source is about a different assessment number
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה and the ברייתא seem to disagree about whether one assessment can ever cover two לאוין
steps.terutzMaskana: An assessment of 41 gives only 39 lashes, so it covers one לאו (the ברייתא). An assessment of 42 gives 39+3, so it covers both (the משנה).

steps.title: How the person is tied and the strap is made
steps.stepSummary: The new משנה describes how the person is tied to a post, how his chest is uncovered, where the attendant stands, and what the strap looks like.
steps.simpleTranslation: How do they flog him? They tie his two hands to a post, one on each side. The חזן הכנסת takes hold of his clothes. If they rip, they rip, and if they come apart, they come apart, until his chest is bare. A stone is placed behind him, and the חזן הכנסת stands on it holding a strap of calf hide. The strap is folded from one into two and from two into four, with two donkey-hide straps going up and down along it. Its handle is a טפח long and it is a טפח wide, and its end reaches the top of his belly.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It explains the practical way מלקות is given, starting with how the person is prepared and what strap is used.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the sugya dealt with how many lashes are given. Now the משנה moves to the actual procedure. The clothes are not handled gently, the person must be firmly held, and the strap has exact measurements so that it reaches from his back around to the front of his belly.

keyTerms.meaning: How do they give lashes
A post or pillar the person is tied to
The attendant of the congregation, who carries out the lashes
A leather strap
A handbreadth, a measurement of length
The top of his belly, near the navel

phrases.english: MISHNA: How do they flog him?
He ties his two hands to the post,
on this side and on that side,
and the attendant of the congregation takes hold of his clothes.
If they ripped, they ripped,
and if they came apart at the seams, they came apart,
until he uncovers his chest.
And the stone is placed behind him.
The attendant of the congregation stands on it
with a strap in his hand, made of calf hide,
folded one into two, and two into four,
and two straps of donkey hide
go up and down along it.
Its handle is a handbreadth, and its width is a handbreadth,
and its end reaches the top of his belly.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה about the procedure of מלקות
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The person is tied to a post with his chest bared, and the attendant stands on a stone behind him holding a folded calf-hide strap of set measurements.

steps.title: Where he is struck and how he is positioned
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says one third of the lashes are on the front and two thirds on the back, and the person must be bent over, based on a פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: He strikes him one third of the lashes on the front, and two thirds on the back. He does not strike him while he is standing or sitting, only while he is bent over, as it says: 'And the judge shall make him lie down.'
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues the procedure. It explains how the lashes are split between front and back, and what position the person must be in.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The lashes are divided into three parts: one part in front and two parts behind. The position comes from the פסוק 'והפילו השופט', which shows he must be close to lying down. That is why he is bent over, not standing upright or sitting.

keyTerms.meaning: One third
Two portions, meaning two thirds
Bent over or leaning, close to lying down
'And the judge shall make him lie down', the source for the bent-over position

phrases.english: And he strikes him one third from the front
and two portions from behind.
phrases.notes: 'Two portions' means two thirds of the lashes, given on his back.

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵינוֹ מַכֶּה אוֹתוֹ לֹא עוֹמֵד וְלֹא יוֹשֵׁב,
phrases.english: And he does not strike him standing or sitting,
but only bent over,
as it is said: 'And the judge shall make him lie down.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same משנה's description of the procedure
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One third of the lashes go on the front and two thirds on the back, and the person must be bent over, based on 'והפילו השופט'.

steps.title: The strike and the verses read aloud
steps.stepSummary: The attendant strikes with one hand and full strength, while a reader recites set פסוקים and starts them over as needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: The one striking strikes with one hand, with all his strength. The reader reads: 'If you do not take care to do...' and 'Then ה׳ will make your plagues extraordinary, and the plagues...', and goes back to the start of the reading. He also reads 'And you shall keep the words of this covenant...', and ends with 'And He is merciful, He atones for sin...', and then goes back to the start of the reading again.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה finishes describing the procedure. It tells us how hard the strike is and which פסוקים are read aloud during the lashes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The lashes are not just a physical punishment. They come together with פסוקים about keeping the תורה and about punishment. The reading ends with 'והוא רחום יכפר עון', so the person hears that ה׳ forgives. The reader keeps going in a loop as long as the lashes continue.

keyTerms.meaning: With all his strength
The reader who recites the פסוקים during the lashes
'He will make extraordinary', said about the plagues in the פסוק
'And He is merciful, He atones for sin', the closing פסוק
Goes back to the beginning of the reading

steps.whatToRemember: מלקות has a fixed procedure: he is tied to a post, struck with a special strap, one third on the front and two thirds on the back, while bent over, and set פסוקים that end with mercy are read the whole time.

and the reader reads:

and he goes back to the beginning of the reading:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the משנה's description of the procedure
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The attendant strikes with one hand and full strength, while a reader recites set פסוקים ending with 'והוא רחום' and starts them over again.

steps.title: Death during lashes versus death from an extra lash
steps.stepSummary: If the person dies from the lashes the court ordered, the attendant is פטור. If the attendant adds even one extra lash and the person dies, the attendant goes into גלות.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the person being whipped dies while the attendant is hitting him, the attendant is exempt. If the attendant gave him one extra lash beyond the amount and he died, the attendant must go into exile because of him.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues describing מלקות and now tells us who is responsible if the person being whipped dies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The attendant who gives only the lashes the court set is just following the בית דין's orders, so he is not blamed if the person dies. Once he gives even one lash beyond that amount, he is acting on his own. If the person dies, the attendant is treated like an accidental killer who must go into גלות.

keyTerms.meaning: Exempt; not held responsible
Literally 'under his hand' — while the attendant is hitting him
Goes into exile to an עיר מקלט, the punishment for killing someone by accident
He added, meaning one more lash than the court ordered

steps.confusionAlert: The word פטור here is about the attendant, not the person being whipped. In the next line, פטור is about the person being whipped.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that even a court-ordered punishment has strict limits. One lash too many is no longer the court's punishment. It counts as harming another person.

phrases.english: And if he dies under his hand – he is exempt.
phrases.notes: The one who dies is the person being whipped. The one who is exempt is the attendant doing the hitting.

phrases.aramaic: הוֹסִיף לוֹ עוֹד רְצוּעָה אַחַת וּמֵת –
phrases.english: If he added for him one more strap-lash and he died –
this one goes into exile on his account.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה's description of how the attendant gives the lashes. Now it covers the result if the person dies.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An attendant who stays within the court's number of lashes is פטור if the person dies. If he adds even one lash and the person dies, he is גולה.

steps.title: Soiling oneself during the lashes ends the punishment
steps.stepSummary: If the person being whipped soils himself, with either excrement or urine, he is exempt from the rest of the lashes. רבי יהודה says a man is only exempt with excrement, and a woman is exempt even with urine.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the person soiled himself, whether with excrement or with urine, he is exempt from the rest of the lashes. רבי יהודה says: a man is exempt only if he soils himself with excrement, and a woman is exempt even with urine.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a second case. If the person being whipped soils himself, we stop the lashes. רבי יהודה disagrees about which kind of soiling counts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Soiling himself in front of everyone is so embarrassing that it counts in place of the rest of the lashes. The תנא קמא says either kind of soiling is enough for anyone. רבי יהודה says it depends on the person: a man is exempt only with excrement, while a woman is exempt even with urine.

keyTerms.meaning: Literally 'became spoiled' — he soiled himself
Excrement
Literally 'water' — here it means urine
The first, unnamed opinion in the משנה, which רבי יהודה argues with

steps.whatToRemember: Two endings to מלקות: (1) The attendant is פטור if the person dies from the set lashes, but גולה if he added a lash. (2) If the person soils himself, the rest of the lashes are cancelled. רבי יהודה says this works differently for a man and a woman.
steps.confusionAlert: Here פטור means the person being whipped is excused from the remaining lashes. It is not about the attendant, as it was in the previous line.

phrases.aramaic: נִתְקַלְקֵל, בֵּין בְּרֵיעִי בֵּין בְּמַיִם – פָּטוּר,
phrases.english: If he soiled himself, whether with excrement or with urine – he is exempt,
Rabbi Yehuda says:
The man – with excrement, and the woman – with urine.

steps.triggerLanguage: נִתְקַלְקֵל, בֵּין בְּרֵיעִי בֵּין בְּמַיִם – פָּטוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second case in which the lashes stop early. This time the reason is the person's embarrassment, not his death.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the person soils himself, he is exempt from the remaining lashes. The תנא קמא says excrement or urine both count. רבי יהודה says a man needs excrement, while for a woman urine is enough.
